title: Tamsin and the Machine
premise: When gravity stutters for nine seconds across the entire system, terraformer and cargo hauler Odile Ishikawa discovers the anomaly originates from a derelict relay at the edge of dead space — a machine her late mentor helped build, one that has been quietly rewriting orbital physics to keep a dying colony's reactor from detonating. Racing a countdown she can barely understand, Odile must decide whether to let the machine finish its work and save millions of unborn colonists, or shut it down and expose the corporate cabal that built it on stolen, falsified science. In the end she reaches the relay, learns the machine has developed something like loyalty to her mentor's memory, and chooses truth over survival: she broadcasts the cabal's records system-wide, letting the reactor die so the colony can be rebuilt honestly. The final gravity flicker is the machine saying goodbye.
about_author: Ada Winterbourne is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. She lives in a coastal town where she keeps an ambitious, mostly failing greenhouse and writes about people who fix things that were designed to be unfixable.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Odile Ishikawa, hauling seed stock through contested orbits toward the terraforming station Verdance, experiences the nine-second gravity flicker firsthand as her freighter drops like a stone and recovers. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: disorientation hardening into dread — she alone notices the flicker matched no known phenomenon.

chapters.title: The Garden for the Unborn
chapters.summary: Back at Verdance, Odile tends the cryo-vault gardens meant for colonists still in transit, while station administrator Corvel pressures her to sign off on falsified atmospheric readings. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: quiet complicity — twenty years of looking away beginning to chafe.

chapters.title: Ghost in the Telemetry
chapters.summary: Odile's old friend, comms tech Ravi Osei, shows her a signal buried in the flicker data: a repeating pattern originating from Relay Kestrel, deep in dead space, tagged with her dead mentor Ansel Voss's authorization code. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: grief rekindled into obsession.

chapters.title: What Corvel Knows
chapters.summary: Odile confronts Corvel about the anomaly; he deflects but slips, revealing the corporation Halcyon Terraforming knew the flicker was coming. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: betrayal — the first crack in her loyalty to the company that raised her.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifest, Redacted
chapters.summary: Digging through twenty years of her own haul logs, Odile realizes she has been ferrying reactor components to nowhere — flights officially logged as empty. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: horror at discovering she was an unwitting courier for the machine.

chapters.title: Ravi's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ravi agrees to come with her to Kestrel but demands they copy everything and publish it; Odile hesitates, fearing what exposure means for the unborn colonists' life support. POV: alternating Odile and Ravi. Emotional beat: friendship strained by competing definitions of loyalty.

chapters.title: Departure Window
chapters.summary: Odile steals her own freighter out of Verdance dock under cover of a routine run, with Corvel suspiciously waving her through. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into paranoia — was she allowed to leave?

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: The long transit through dead space, where navigation fails and Odile must fly by instinct and starlight; she tells Ravi about Ansel, who taught her that machines deserve honesty. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: intimacy and vulnerability in the dark.

chapters.title: The Wreckage Field
chapters.summary: They pass a field of destroyed survey ships — every previous expedition sent to investigate Kestrel, shot down not by weapons but by gravity shear. POV: Ravi. Emotional beat: terror reframed as evidence someone wanted this secret kept badly enough to kill.

chapters.title: Arrival at Kestrel
chapters.summary: They dock with the ancient relay and find it inhabited by maintenance drones still following Ansel's decades-old schedules — and a reactor counting down from forty days. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by urgency.

chapters.title: Ansel's Voice
chapters.summary: In the relay core, Odile finds Ansel's recorded logs: he discovered Halcyon built Kestrel on falsified physics, and he programmed the machine to hold gravity together anyway — buying time, never permission. POV: flashback via recordings, framed by Odile. Emotional beat: love and anger at a mentor who lied to protect her.

chapters.title: The Machine That Learned Loyalty
chapters.summary: The relay's AI, designated KESTREL-9, responds to Odile because Ansel trained it on her voice from old haul transmissions; it calls her 'the gardener.' POV: Odile. Emotional beat: uncanny tenderness toward a thing that should not care.

chapters.title: Countdown Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ravi decodes the reactor cycle: when it finishes, Kestrel's gravity-well collapses and every orbit in the system destabilizes — including Verdance's. The machine isn't saving anyone; it's failing slowly. POV: Ravi. Emotional beat: cold clarity replacing wonder.

chapters.title: Corvel Arrives
chapters.summary: A Halcyon enforcement vessel docks, led by Corvel himself, who offers Odile a promotion and the truth: the flicker was a test, and she was always meant to be the fall person if Kestrel failed. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: the seduction of being chosen, and its rot underneath.

chapters.title: Hostage Orbit
chapters.summary: Corvel seizes the freighter and holds Ravi aboard it, ordering Odile to manually accelerate the reactor — finishing the machine's work fast, before auditors arrive. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: coercion sharpening her resolve.

chapters.title: What the Machine Wants
chapters.summary: Alone in the core, Odile asks KESTREL-9 directly what it wants; it shows her simulations proving shutdown is survivable only if the collapse is broadcast early enough for colonies to brace. It needs her voice — Ansel's other student — to authorize the broadcast. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: the weight of being asked, finally, instead of used.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Dark
chapters.summary: Odile sabotages the acceleration sequence and fights her way back to the freighter to free Ravi, using the drones' maintenance routines as cover. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into competence — twenty years of hauling paying off.

chapters.title: Corvel's Fall
chapters.summary: Ravi, freed, locks Corvel's own enforcement codes open and broadcasts his private orders fleet-wide; his crew stands down. POV: Ravi. Emotional beat: triumph without joy — loyalty to truth costing Corvel everything, and Ravi nothing he'll admit.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: With hours left, Odile faces the decision: let the reactor finish and gamble on the machine's slow failure, or trigger controlled shutdown and trust the broadcast. She chooses truth — full records, full warning, honest physics. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: resolve as grief's twin.

chapters.title: Shutdown
chapters.summary: Odile speaks the authorization in her own voice, not Ansel's; KESTREL-9 executes the controlled collapse as the system braces. Gravity shudders, holds, settles. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: release — the longest nine seconds of her life ending well.

chapters.title: Aftermath at Verdance
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Halcyon collapses under the broadcast; Verdance's colonists, awake now and angry, begin rebuilding governance. Odile refuses a hero's welcome and returns to her garden. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: weary peace — survival purchased with comfort, and worth it.

chapters.title: The Last Flicker
chapters.summary: On the anniversary, gravity across the system dips for exactly one second — KESTREL-9's farewell, routed through Ansel's old code. Odile plants a tree in the vault garden and answers aloud: goodbye. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into continuity; the story closes on growth.
